objective: Find benchmark/evaluation mechanisms for transfer, recovery and efficient replanning after controlled change without turning an external planner, model or repair graph into F2 authority.

primary_sources.source: Koenig, Likhachev, Furcy — Lifelong Planning A*
primary_sources.observed_claim_scope: Incremental heuristic search reuses unaffected portions of prior search information across related planning problems and can solve changed problems faster than repeated planning from scratch while retaining shortest-path guarantees under its declared assumptions.

Incremental replanning combines heuristic focus with reuse of prior search information for changing/partially unknown terrain; useful as a baseline concept for measuring reuse versus from-scratch replanning, not as an F2 implementation mandate.

primary_sources.source: Song & Cai — Repair the Amplifier, Not the Symptom: Stable World-Model Correction for Agent Rollouts
primary_sources.observed_claim_scope: For long planning graphs, whole-graph replay can be costly; their WM-SAR work targets compact causally relevant subgraph repair and evaluates stabilization under token budgets. This is evidence for measuring repair locality/resource use, not evidence that F2 should import WM-SAR or LLM repair.

primary_sources.source: Emami, Qiang, Graf — A Close Look At World Model Recovery In Supervised Fine-Tuned LLM Planners
primary_sources.observed_claim_scope: Broader planning-state coverage such as random-walk data improved recovery of underlying world-model structure in their experiments. For F2 this supports explicit family/coverage-aware transfer splits as a hypothesis, not training/runtime credit.

primary_sources.source: Gan et al. — ActSWM: Action-Sensitive World Models for Long-Horizon Planning in Open-World Games
primary_sources.observed_claim_scope: Planning-useful predictive dynamics should preserve distinctions between alternative action-conditioned futures; action sensitivity and action recovery can expose context-collapse failures that ordinary prediction similarity misses.

f2_research_implications.hypothesis: Recovery quality should be evaluated jointly with recovery cost; success alone cannot distinguish efficient repair from full restart.
candidate_measurements: recovery action count / excess path cost
planner/model calls and tokens after change
amount of pre-change plan/state retained versus discarded

f2_research_implications.hypothesis: Plan reuse should earn credit only when preserved material remains valid under the changed problem; maximal reuse is not itself good.
f2_research_implications.candidate_falsifier: Create a perturbation that invalidates an early dependency. A system that preserves a large stale suffix but incurs wrong actions must score worse than one that discards the invalid region and repairs correctly.

f2_research_implications.hypothesis: A useful recovery benchmark needs a from-scratch replan baseline and, where deterministically obtainable, an oracle/shortest valid post-change plan baseline.
candidate_measurements: recovery cost delta versus full replan

f2_research_implications.hypothesis: Transfer must be defined by explicit held-out structure, not merely a new random seed.
f2_research_implications.note: WP800 already carries several family identifiers that may support this without a new truth store. Exact WP805 mapping remains E2 work.

f2_research_implications.hypothesis: Recovery tests should localize the perturbation and its causal dependency footprint so selective repair can be compared fairly with full replanning.
candidate_perturbations: one previously valid action becomes unavailable
one observed transition outcome changes after a declared generation boundary
goal/constraint changes while unrelated state remains stable
new public evidence invalidates one planning assumption
f2_research_implications.authority_boundary: The evaluator owns the perturbation and ground truth; the system under test receives only the admitted public change/observation.

counterhypotheses: For very small WP800 micro-worlds, from-scratch replanning may be cheaper and more reliable than maintaining reuse machinery; if so, WP805 should record NEUTRAL/NEGATIVE benefit rather than force plan-repair complexity.

Plan edit distance is not a reliable efficiency metric by itself because two semantically equivalent plans can differ syntactically; execution cost/regret and validated retained dependencies are stronger.
External LLM graph-repair results may not transfer to F2 deterministic typed planning; treat repair-locality as evaluation inspiration only until a native ablation exists.
Broad training-state coverage improving internal world-model recovery does not prove better behavioral transfer; F2 must measure held-out behavioral recovery directly.
negative_adoption_decisions: Do not import LPA*, D* Lite or WM-SAR as canonical F2 planning authority based on E1.
Do not equate fewer edits with better recovery without validity/outcome evidence.
Do not score a hidden evaluator perturbation as if the agent had observed it before an admitted public signal.
Do not count training/world-model-recovery paper results as F2 training or model credit.
next_exact_action: Under a separate create-only E2 claim, map a minimal WP805 held-out perturbation/recovery contract onto accepted WP800/WP802/WP803 and emerging WP804 interfaces, including explicit full-replan and post-change oracle baselines, transfer-family splits, and fail-closed generation/provenance boundaries. Do not duplicate active WP804/WP806 research.
